summary: Pixel blit that copies a rectangular region from a 16-bit source pixel buffer to a 32-bit destination buffer, expanding each 16-bit pixel into a 32-bit word by duplicating it into the low and high halves. Rows of a9 source words are processed; a pixel equal to the reference color a11 is skipped (color-key / transparency). Per-source-word dest stride is doubled (a9 *= 2) because each word becomes two bytes written as one dword pair. Address arithmetic is built from flat base/stride/count parameters rather than surface structs, so the exact buffer layouts are not evidenced.

operations.description: Store the reference color a11 into v17; it is compared against each source pixel to decide whether to write.
Double the source row word-count a9 (a9 *= 2); used both as the inner-loop counter and in dest pointer stepping because each source word expands to a 32-bit dword.
Compute the source row start as a word pointer: v11 = (a1 + 2*a2 + a3*a4), mixing a base pointer a1, a byte stride a2, and row index a3 over a4 columns.
Compute the destination row start as a dword pointer: v12 = 2*a6 + a7*a8, then v13 = a5 + v12.
Seed the inner pixel counter v14 = a9 and precompute the source row-advance correction v18 = a4 - a9.

Capture the prior dest row stride v15 = _InterlockedExchange(&a8, 2*(a8 - a9)): a8 is updated to the per-row byte advance and its old value (the second-write offset) is kept in v15. The exchange on a stack parameter is almost certainly a decompiler artifact of a plain assignment.
Nested loop: inner loop writes a9 source words per row; on row end the outer loop advances both pointers and continues while a10 rows remain (break when a10 <= 1 after the decrement).
Skip the pixel when it equals the reference color: write only if v17 != *v11 (color-key / transparency test).
Expand the 16-bit pixel to 32 bits by duplicating it into the low and high words of v12, then write two dwords: *v13 = v12 and *(v13 + v15) = v12.
Advance per pixel: ++v11 and ++v13, and decrement the inner counter v14 by 2 (two words consumed per dest dword).
Row end: reset v14 = a9, advance the source row by v18 words and the dest row by the new a8, then decrement the row counter a10 and exit when a10 <= 1.

unresolved: Source surface layout (a1/a2/a3/a4) and destination surface layout (a5/a6/a7/a8) are flat parameters, not structs; their exact semantics are unproven.
Why two dest dwords are written per source word (v15 = prior a8 offset) is unclear; possibly two interleaved dest buffers or a double-write pattern.
The _InterlockedExchange on stack parameter a8 is likely a decompiler artifact; the real write is probably a plain assignment.
The reference color a11 is inferred as a color-key/transparency value from the guard, but that role is not named by the evidence.
